title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-iam-networking-migration
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Unify Terraform state layout for Private deployments: reorganizes GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking modules; provides an automated migration path; backward-compatible by default with opt-in switchover.
description: Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated multiple divergent Terraform state layouts across GPU node pools, IAM, and networking modules. This makes upgrades, cross-region replication, and automated installs brittle and error-prone. This PR unifies the state layout and module boundaries for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments to standardize lifecycle operations and enable safer automated migrations for customers running GPU workloads. Summary of changes: - Introduces a unified state layout under modules/state/remote_state.tf and new namespaced workspaces for private deployments. - Consolidates GPU node pool configuration into modules/gpu_node_pool with clearer inputs for accelerator_family, instance_types, autoscaling_policy, and taints. - Extracts and normalizes IAM roles/policies used by private control-plane and node pools into modules/iam/roles.tf and modules/iam/policies.tf. - Moves VPC and subnet management into modules/networking/vpc.tf with optional network-peering and route tables for cross-region private clusters. - Adds migration helpers in scripts/migrate/private_state_migrate.sh and tests in tests/terraform/upgrade_test.sh. - Adds an examples/private-deploy/README.md with step-by-step migration guide and rollback instructions. Migration plan (high level): 1) Dry-run: run terraform plan against the new layout using the provided migration script which maps old state objects into the new namespaced workspace layout. 2) Canary: apply the new layout in a test/private canary account (documented in examples) and validate node pool scaling, IAM policy attachments, and networking connectivity. 3) Rollout: incrementally migrate production workspaces with automated verification and an automated alias back to the legacy layout if validation fails. Backwards compatibility and risk: - Default behavior is opt-in: existing state remains unchanged until operators run the migration helper. - The migration script creates backups of remote state and emits a mapping file for audit. - The module remains backward compatible with existing Terraform variable names where possible; several deprecated variables are flagged with deprecation messages and mapped internally. Testing and CI: - Added unit-style terraform validation runs and an integration-style upgrade_test.sh that exercises node pool creation, IAM role attachment, and VPC route propagation in a mocked environment. - CI initially failed lint/validate on a couple of naming collisions; those were fixed in follow-up commits. Rollback: - The migration script writes state backups and a reverse-mapping. To rollback, operators can restore the previous remote state snapshot and re-run terraform apply against the legacy layout. Follow-ups: - Add automated telemetry for migration success/failure to the internal migrations dashboard (ENG-4890). - Add docs for on-prem installer edge cases (MTU, VLAN) in a separate PR. See changed files for a concise list and review thread for detailed comments and decisions.
